title: Endpoint Contracts & Operational Launch Checklist for Unified Hosted Inference
creator: Mariana Ruiz
summary: PRD that defines functional contracts, operational SLAs, and an end-to-end launch checklist for the unified hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). This ticket consolidates behavior expectations, rollout safeguards, compatibility guarantees, and acceptance criteria to enable a coordinated launch across runtime, console, and SDK teams.
background: We are consolidating multiple inference surfaces into a single hosted API offering to reduce developer confusion and operational burden. Prior PRDs focused on separate endpoint bundles; this doc captures the cross-cutting operational contracts (timeouts, fallbacks, modality compatibility) and a prescriptive launch checklist so we don't regress on latency or quality during rollout.
goals: Define deterministic endpoint behavior across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank for parity with existing surfaces
Establish clear acceptance criteria for latency, error budgets, and quality regressions
Provide an actionable launch checklist that coordinates runtime, SDKs, console, docs, and on-call
Minimize customer impact during rollout with automated fallbacks and staged ramping
out_of_scope: New model onboarding workflows (handled by model-onboarding epic)
Billing model changes and pricing experiments
Deep changes to inference kernels and quantization—performance patches only
scope_in_scope: API surface contract definitions for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Behavioral guarantees for streaming, function-calling, and structured output
Operational SLOs and observability knobs required for launch
A rollout plan including canary percentages, rollback triggers, and fallback mappings
requirements: Public API: single /v1/inference endpoint with 'mode' parameter (chat|completion|embed|rerank) and documented behavior per mode
Backward compatibility: existing /v1/chat and /v1/completions endpoints must remain operational until v2 deprecation plan is complete
Streaming semantics: streaming must deliver partial tokens in order and include explicit 'done' event when complete
Function/tool-calling: must support tool result injection and strict schema validation errors surfaced with 4xx
Embeddings determinism: stable vector dimensionality and documented normalization behavior
Rerank contract: deterministic score range and tie-breaking policy documented
Timeouts: default request timeout 60s, configurable per-API key with maximum 300s
Rate limits and quotas: per-token and per-request limits defined; error responses include retry-after where appropriate
Fallbacks: runtime must map unavailable heavy models to lighter variants with documented quality delta
Observability: token-level cost, per-request latency, model variant tag, and KV cache-hit metrics emitted to console and traces
acceptance_criteria: Functional: each mode passes mode-specific smoke tests (see links) against the staging environment
Performance: median P50 latency for small prompt (<=128 tokens) <= 80ms for completions, <=120ms for chat; P95 within two times median
Throughput: dedicated autoscale profile can maintain 400 qps sustained on target Dedicated size without queueing beyond 100ms
Reliability: error budget consumption < 0.5% during 72h canary at 5% traffic
Quality: embeddings cosine similarity regression < 0.5% against baseline dataset (50k pairs), rerank NDCG drop < 1%
Streaming correctness: stream reassembly tests pass for interleaved part ordering and reconnect scenarios
Security & Compliance: KMS integration validated for private deployments and SSO guards for console settings
Docs & SDKs: examples for each mode are present in SDKs and docs with runnable quickstarts
Rollout automation: automatic rollback triggers implemented in console and verified on staging (latency/error thresholds)
Sign-offs: PM, Runtime Eng, SDK, Docs, Security, and Support have approved the launch checklist
rollout_plan: Canary stage: 1% traffic for 24h -> check SLOs and logs; if error budget breached, auto rollback
Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 72h with manual gating at each step
Regional ramp: launch in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 first, then ap-southeast-1 after regional health checks
Model fallback mapping: if model variant X degrades, auto-route to Y with telemetry tag 'fallback=<reason>'
Deprecation path: maintain legacy endpoints with a compatibility proxy for 90 days while informing customers
launch_checklist: Runtime: health checks + synthetic workload showing latency & KV cache hit rates within targets
Console: route and rollout UI controls present; cost attribution surfaced per model/route
SDKs: v1.9 release with new mode enum and sample apps published to npm/pypi
Docs: PRD-derived behavioral contracts published to docs.redwood.ai, quickstart for each mode
Open-source examples: reference repo updated with migration guide
Observability: dashboards for P50/P95 latency, errors, fallback events, and token-level cost wired to alerts
On-call runbook: escalation steps and rollback commands documented and accessible
Security: KMS test vector verified; audit log entries confirmed for key operations
Legal/Compliance: SOC/ISO sign-off on hosted-api changes (if required)
Support: canned responses and troubleshooting playbook created; Support trained via internal session
Customer communications: migration email + changelog entry scheduled; sample migration code snippets included
Performance load test: pass 95% of test scenarios for target qps on Dedicated/Hosted profiles
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regression when mapping to lighter model variants. Mitigation: require quality gate checks and automatic rollback triggers if user-facing metrics degrade.
Risk: Unanticipated latency spikes during ramp. Mitigation: phased ramp + synthetic canary tests + pre-warm caches
Risk: SDK breaking changes. Mitigation: maintain compatibility layer in SDKs and publish migration guide with examples
Risk: Billing mismatch causing customer confusion. Mitigation: cost-per-token labeling in console and invoice-preview tests
Risk: Security sign-off delays. Mitigation: prioritize KMS/HSM integration tests early and allocate security review slot in sprint
open_questions: Should we expose a per-request 'preferred_model' hint that can be ignored by routing policies? (trade-off: customer control vs scheduling complexity)
What is the exact deprecation cadence for /v1/chat and /v1/completions? Propose 90 days with telemetry-driven extension
Do we require separate SLOs for streaming vs non-streaming paths? (proposal: yes; streaming SLOs measured end-to-end)
What tenant-level controls are required for customers to opt out of fallback routing?
